subject: chemistry
title: Periodicity Adventure 2: Period 3 oxides and chlorides
welcome_lead: Today you'll burn period 3 elements and watch their oxides shift from basic to acidic.
meta_desc: Chemistry — period 3 oxides, ionic vs covalent, acidic/basic behaviour, chlorides.
final_note: You learned period 3 oxides trend ionic basic (Na₂O, MgO) → amphoteric (Al₂O₃) → covalent acidic (SO₃, P₄O₁₀), reflecting bond type and electronegativity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Across period 3:

- Na, Mg, Al — ionic bonding with O²⁻.
- Si — giant covalent SiO₂ (sand, quartz).
- P, S, Cl — molecular covalent (P₄O₁₀, SO₃, Cl₂O).

Electronegativity gap with O shrinks across → bonding switches from ionic to covalent.

- Basic: Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH (pH 14).
- Basic: MgO sparingly soluble (pH ~10).
- Amphoteric: Al₂O₃ reacts with HCl and NaOH.
- Acidic: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄ (pH ~0).
- Acidic: P₄O₁₀ + 6H₂O → 4H₃PO₄.

NaCl, MgCl₂ — ionic, dissolve in water (neutral or slightly acidic).

AlCl₃ — covalent dimer Al₂Cl₆; reacts with water giving HCl + Al(OH)₃, acidic pH ~3.

SiCl₄, PCl₃, PCl₅, SCl₂ — all fume in moist air, hydrolyse giving HCl + oxoacid.

This trend illustrates the link between bonding character and reactivity.

mcqs.q: Na₂O reacts with water to give a solution of pH approximately:
What does the M+ peak in a mass spectrum represent?
options: The M+ peak shows the mass of the largest fragment after the molecule breaks apart.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
The molecular ion — formed when a single electron is removed from the whole molecule, giving the relative molecular mass.
The M+ peak shows the mass of a single hydrogen atom added to the molecule.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
The M+ peak shows the mass of a single hydrogen atom added to the molecule.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.

mcqs.q: Why is the 4s orbital filled before the 3d orbital?
options: Because the 4s shell is closer to the nucleus than the 3d shell.
Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
Because the 4s orbital has a lower energy than 3d when both are empty, so electrons fill it first.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
